snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson on Michael Sequel: “I’ll Be Ready Once They Tell Me to Go” | Newport Beach Film
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson speaks with Entertainment Tonight at the 27th Newport Beach Film Festival Honors, where he was recognized as one of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch for 2026.

In this interview, he opens up about how the success of the first Michael film has given him more confidence and ease when approaching a role of that magnitude. He also shares an update on the sequel, confirming that it is still in the early talks, while expressing his readiness: “I’ll be ready once they tell me to go.”

The first film, released in April 2026, went on to become the first biopic in history to cross $1 billion worldwide.

Credits: Entertainment Tonight

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Shares His Thoughts After Receiving Variety Honor | Newport Beach Interview
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson shares his most unforgettable moment from making "Michael": filming in Michael Jackson's real bedroom at the Havenhurst family home in Encino, California. The room was decorated exactly how Michael had it. Before shooting, Jaafar would sometimes walk onto the set, sit quietly, and take in the room to feel the energy. He says, "It was like a spiritual experience for me."

This interview was filmed by the Newport Beach Film Festival at the 27th Newport Beach Film Festival Honors brunch on Sunday, 18 October 2026, at the Balboa Bay Resort in Newport Beach, California, where Jaafar was honored as one of Variety's 10 Actors to Watch for 2026.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Receives a Traditional Māori Welcome in New Zealand (1996) #shorts
snippet.description:
On 8 November 1996, Michael Jackson arrived at the Carlton Hotel in Auckland, New Zealand, for his HIStory World Tour shows and was welcomed with a traditional Māori pōwhiri (welcome ceremony).

He walked in with New Zealand entertainer Sir Howard Morrison as conch shells were blown. A Māori warrior then performed the wero, a challenge that checks whether a visitor comes in peace. Michael picked up the taki (a token placed in front of him), which means "I come in peace." He then greeted the warriors with a hongi, the traditional Māori greeting where two people press their noses and foreheads together, sharing the "breath of life."

A beautiful moment of respect between the King of Pop and Māori culture. ❤️🇳🇿

Footage from two camera angles of the same welcome.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson's Real Costumes in Japan 🇯🇵 Light-Up Thriller Jacket, Smooth Criminal Suit & More
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s real stage costumes and iconic pieces went on display in Osaka, Japan ahead of a major auction.

From 9–12 October 2026, Hankyu Umeda Main Store in Osaka hosted the special preview exhibition “Hankyu & Julien’s Presents Michael Jackson & Princess Diana Auction Exhibition” in partnership with Julien’s Auctions. Around 30–50 items connected to Michael Jackson and Princess Diana were shown.

One of the biggest highlights was the light-up red-and-black “Thriller” jacket from the Bad Tour (1988). Michael Jackson’s longtime costume designer Michael Bush was present and switched the lights on — the first time the jacket had been illuminated since 1988. The jacket was designed so the lights moved in sync with the beat of “Thriller.”

Other notable pieces on display included:

➣The cream “Smooth Criminal” suit (with blue pinstripes) from the 1988 music video
➣The Motown 25 (1983) rhinestone glove and related loafers
➣Outfits and pieces from the Bad Tour, Dangerous Tour, Moonwalker, Black or White, and the 30th Anniversary concert
➣Shoes, gloves, masks, and other stage accessories

These costumes are part of the largest collection of Michael Jackson stage wear and video-worn pieces ever brought together by Julien’s Auctions.

The main auction is happening in Abu Dhabi.

Julien’s Auctions is holding Michael Jackson: The Fashion Legacy Auction on 7 December 2026 at Rosewood Abu Dhabi, as part of its Celebrity & Pop Culture Experience (running roughly 7–9 December 2026). Headline lots include the original 1983 “Thriller” music video jacket and the Motown 25 rhinestone glove (estimated at $600,000–$800,000).

These pieces are a big part of music and fashion history. Which costume is your favourite? Let me know in the comments 👇

📸 Photos and clips: Fans who attended the Osaka exhibition (shared on X)

snippet.title: Believe In Yourself – Michael Jackson's Most Powerful Message (2003) ✨
snippet.description:
Some words never get old. Michael spoke these lines in 2003, in a home video filmed with Brett Ratner, and they still hit just as hard today.

"Believe in yourself. Study the greats and become greater… I don't care if the whole world is against you… Believe in yourself, no matter what. They laughed at the Wright brothers. They laughed at Thomas Edison. They laughed at Walt Disney."

He wasn't just talking about music. He was talking about every dream people laugh at before the world finally understands it. "Study the greats and become greater" is something he truly lived by. He learned from legends and then became one himself.

Whatever you're working towards right now, keep going. ✨

Voice: Michael Jackson, home video with Brett Ratner (2003)

snippet.title: Kids Sing “We Are the World” for Michael Jackson | Gardner School 1989
snippet.description:
Kids sing "We Are the World" for Michael Jackson at his old school 🎶

In October 1989, Michael returned to Gardner Street Elementary School in Hollywood, where he studied in 6th grade, the last public school he attended before fame took over. That day, the school dedicated its auditorium in his name, and during the ceremony the school choir sang "We Are the World," the song he co-wrote with Lionel Richie. Michael said he was deeply touched that the auditorium where he once sat as a child was now dedicated to him, adding that "the children are our future." He stayed connected to the school afterwards, paying its music teacher's salary, planting rose bushes near the playground, and even signing the wall of his old 6th grade classroom.

snippet.title: MJ Working on the 9/11 Charity Song (Studio Session)
snippet.description:
Rare 2001 studio footage of Michael Jackson working on “What More Can I Give” — the charity song he wrote after the 9/11 attacks.

The song was created to support the victims and their families. Michael brought together major artists including Beyoncé, Celine Dion, Mariah Carey, Usher, Luther Vandross, and many others. Sessions were recorded in Los Angeles and other locations around the world, coordinated by Marc Schaffel using Michael’s private plane and mobile studio.

Despite the effort, Sony never properly released the song at the time. Watching him guide the vocals shows how much heart and perfection he put into this project 🤍

snippet.title: Invincible Returns on Grey Marble Vinyl | Michael Jackson
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson's Invincible is back on vinyl, and the first copies of the limited Marbled Stone Grey edition have already reached stores, with pre-orders being packed ahead of release.

The reissue comes in two versions: a standard black 2LP and a limited Marbled Stone Grey 2LP (140g), released to celebrate the album's 25th anniversary. It arrives from 16 October 2026, with the grey edition releasing in the UK on 17 October as part of National Album Day. Release dates may vary by country.

Originally released on 30 October 2001, Invincible was MJ's final studio album and includes You Rock My World, Butterflies and Cry. Lovely to see it finally getting this attention 🖤

Video credit: imusicdk (Instagram)
Song: You Rock My World

snippet.title: Spectacle: Michael Jackson at the Super Bowl | New Documentary Coming February 2027 on Hulu & ESPN
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s legendary 1993 Super Bowl XXVII halftime show at the Rose Bowl is finally getting its own documentary.

“Spectacle: Michael Jackson at the Super Bowl” arrives in February 2027 on Hulu and ESPN, and on Hulu on Disney+ too. The documentary is timed to release just ahead of Super Bowl LXI (February 14, 2027).

It’s directed by Bao Nguyen, the filmmaker behind The Greatest Night in Pop and the Emmy-nominated Bruce Lee documentary Be Water. The film follows Michael as he prepares for the show and includes never-before-seen footage of him and his team.

It also looks at how that one performance — with “Jam,” “Billie Jean,” “Black or White,” “We Are the World,” and “Heal the World” — changed the halftime show forever. Around 133.4 million people watched it, and it was the first time ratings actually went up during the halftime break.

The documentary is produced by Skydance Sports, Optimum Productions, and Into the Deep End Films, with NFL Films involved as executive producer.

It comes after the huge success of Michael (starring Jaafar Jackson), and Michael 2 is already in development, expected between late 2027 and the first half of 2028. 👑

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Takes Paris Shopping on Her 9th Birthday | Las Vegas, April 2007
snippet.description:
On 3 April 2007, Michael Jackson marked his daughter Paris Jackson’s 9th birthday with a private shopping day in Las Vegas.

According to reports published the next day by TMZ and Just Jared, Michael, Paris, Prince, and Michael II (Blanket), with several bodyguards, began at the FAO Schwarz toy store inside the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace. The store was closed for more than an hour so the family could shop in private. TMZ reported that Paris’s face was covered, that matching bodyguards walked with them through Caesars Palace, and that a large crowd followed them to the toy store.

After the toy store, the family went to the Wynn Hotel. They had lunch at the Chinese restaurant Wing Lei, then walked through the Wynn shops. Michael, then 48, stopped at the Rolex store to look at watches.

Just Jared reported that the family later returned home, where a birthday party was held for Paris. Charlie the Clown was among the visitors.

Photographs from the day were credited to Bauer-Griffin.

This clip is from that 3 April 2007 Las Vegas birthday outing, as reported at the time.

Sources: TMZ, 4 April 2007; Just Jared, 4 April 2007.

This is archival fan footage from April 2007. It is shared for historical and fan interest. All rights remain with the original owners.

snippet.title: Paris Jackson Arrives at the BoF 500 Gala 2026 in Paris
snippet.description:
Paris Jackson arrives at The Business of Fashion’s BoF 500 Gala on Saturday, 3 October 2026, at the Shangri-La Paris during Paris Fashion Week. The gala is BoF’s yearly celebration of the people shaping the global fashion industry, and this year it welcomed the newest names on the list. Miuccia Prada, Marc Jacobs, Sarah Burton and Satoshi Kondo are the 2026 cover stars.

snippet.title: Thriller Challenge 2026 | Stream, Buy & Request Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” | Oct 30–Nov 5
snippet.description:
Thriller Challenge 2026 runs from October 30 to November 5, 2026.

The Thriller album spent 37 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The single never did. In 1984 it peaked at No. 4 on the Hot 100, and it has never reached No. 1. Last Halloween it returned to No. 10. This year’s goal is to push “Thriller” up the charts in the United States and worldwide, including the Hot 100 and the Billboard Global 200.

How it counts:
• Stream the full song while logged in, on Spotify, Apple Music, and the other major platforms.

• Use only the official versions from the original Thriller album, Thriller 25, or Thriller 40. Remixes and unofficial uploads do not count

• Offline plays count once you reconnect.

• Buy it on iTunes or Amazon. If you already own it, send an Apple Gift Card so someone else can purchase it.

• Request it on radio, especially the stations that carry the most weight on the Hot 100.

• Join the Stationhead parties linked on the site. Each attendee’s listen counts as an additional stream.

• Do not loop it. Do not use bots or a VPN.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Camel Walk | Billie Jean Live
snippet.description:
I've been seeing so many reels where people ask what this Michael Jackson step is called. The closest name is the Camel Walk, the step-touch with a heel pop that James Brown was known for. James Brown was one of MJ’s biggest inspirations.

MJ does not do it in its pure form. He adds the forward lean, the knee pops and the arm swings, so the step becomes his own version. That is why people keep arguing over the name.

What do you think? Let me know in the comments.

About Billie Jean:
Billie Jean is one of Michael Jackson's most iconic songs, from the album Thriller (1982). Written by Michael Jackson and produced by Quincy Jones, it spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The Motown 25 performance in 1983 became a historic moment, as it was the night the world first saw the moonwalk. After that, Billie Jean remained a highlight of almost every MJ concert.

Credits to the respective owners. No copyright infringement intended.

snippet.title: 1991 Studio Tape: Michael Jackson Choosing the Perfect “Go With It, Jam” Take
snippet.description:
Summer 1991. Michael Jackson and engineer Bruce Swedien are in the control room during the Dangerous sessions, working one line: “Go with it, go with it, jam.”

The takes already sound almost the same. They are listening for timing, breath, emphasis and where the phrase sits on the groove, then marking choices on a paper comp sheet. That process is vocal comping — many lead-vocal passes, with the finished vocal built from selected phrases. In 1991 this was done with tape machines and live faders, before pitch-correction software became standard.

The footage was filmed by Brad Sundberg, assistant engineer and technical director on the album. He has said the team used a 48-track setup with about 46 possible lead-vocal tracks after the headphone mix, and that Jam later grew across multiple locked machines.

The groove began as a demo called “Time Marches On,” made by Bruce Swedien and René Moore. Jackson took the beat to Dangerous. Teddy Riley added keyboards, horns and guitar; Jackson wrote the lyrics.
The song was written and produced by Michael Jackson, Bruce Swedien, Teddy Riley and René Moore, with a rap by Heavy D.

Dangerous was released on 26 November 1991, with “Jam” as the opening track. The short film with Michael Jordan premiered on 19 June 1992; the single followed that summer.

Filmed by Brad Sundberg
Engineered by Bruce Swedien
Dangerous sessions, 1991

Rights remain with the owners. Shared for documentation and education.

snippet.title: Tyla & Miles Caton Name Michael Jackson Music Videos | 2026 VMAs Red Carpet
snippet.description:
Tyla named Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” as the music video she would most like to appear in.

At the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on 27 September at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, Billboard asked celebrities on the red carpet: “If you could be in any music video, what would it be?”

Tyla, who attended as a presenter, chose Michael Jackson’s 1983 short film Thriller. The interview clip shows her answer followed immediately by the famous red-jacket zombie dance sequence.

Miles Caton also named a Michael Jackson music video in the same red-carpet interviews.

Thriller is still the most cited Jackson video in these conversations because of its 14-minute narrative format, choreography, and lasting influence. It won three VMAs in 1984 and is widely regarded as the most important music video ever made.
